children.name: Thematic Coding
children.blurb: Thematic coding is a qualitative analysis technique for identifying, organizing, and interpreting recurring patterns of meaning across text, interview transcripts, field notes, or other unstructured material.

children.name: Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation
children.blurb: Interview transcription and speaker separation covers the conversion of recorded qualitative interviews into text with reliable labels for each speaker.

children.name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
children.blurb: Finding patterns in lived experience refers to systematic analysis of qualitative data such as interviews, diaries, open-ended survey responses, and field notes to identify recurring themes, narratives, and meanings.

children.name: Ethnographic Synthesis
children.blurb: Ethnographic synthesis brings together findings from multiple ethnographic studies to build higher-order interpretations of cultural and social phenomena.

children.name: Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data
children.blurb: Combining qualitative and quantitative data means bringing together non-numeric evidence such as interviews, field notes, documents, or open-ended survey responses with numeric measures, counts, or model outputs.

sections.body: Qualitative analysis and mixed methods in AI research is the study of how machines can help researchers work with words, images, audio and observed behavior rather than only with numbers. In practice, AI now handles interview transcription and speaker separation, suggests codes for passages of text, groups similar excerpts, and helps trace patterns across field notes and archives. It can also support ethnographic synthesis by linking observations to themes and by comparing qualitative findings with quantitative measures. These tools do not replace the researcher's judgment, they change where time is spent, moving effort from mechanical sorting toward interpretation and argument. The work sits inside a broader AI researcher agenda that asks how computational methods can be made accountable to human meaning.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Automatic transcription is the most settled part of this field, and speaker separation works well when audio is clear and speakers do not overlap much. Thematic coding tools can propose labels and retrieve examples, but they do not understand context, irony, silence or the reasons a participant chose a word. Pattern finding across lived experience remains difficult because human accounts are partial, situated and often contradictory, and a model may smooth over exactly those tensions. Ethnographic synthesis is harder still, since it depends on long term immersion, field relationships and tacit knowledge that are rarely captured in a transcript. Combining qualitative and quantitative data is not solved by a single pipeline, because the two kinds of evidence answer different questions and require explicit decisions about weighting, sequence and interpretation. The site's library holds 135 research papers, and the qualitative methods described here often rest on a much smaller set of detailed studies, which is an honest limit on how much can be generalized.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The page on Thematic Coding is the entry point for readers who want to see how labels, categories and codebooks are built and where automation helps or misleads. Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation covers the front end of the pipeline, the step that turns recorded talk into text and marks who said what. Finding Patterns in Lived Experience looks at how researchers search for recurring themes, deviant cases and narrative arcs without reducing people to data points. Ethnographic Synthesis extends that work to field notes, observations and documents, asking how AI can assist with the slow construction of cultural interpretation. Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data shows how the two streams can be joined in a single study, and it is the page to read when the question is about integration rather than coding alone. Together these pages move from raw audio to coded text to interpreted meaning to mixed evidence, and each one names the points where human review remains necessary.
